triggers: a native Metal engine needs a fast quantized GEMM without hand-writing MMA kernels
integrating MLX operators into a non-MLX C++ pipeline

payload.goal: Use mlx::core quantized_matmul as a drop-in backend for a native Metal engine.

problem.target: Apple Silicon (M-series) unified-memory GPU, mlx 0.32 C++ API
problem.statement: Hand-written public-API Metal kernels plateau near ~9 TFLOPS effective on q4 GEMM while MLX reaches ~43 TFLOPS.

payload.what: The mlx wheel ships full C++ headers, libmlx.dylib, and the precompiled mlx.metallib. Link libmlx, register the metallib via mlx::core::metal::set_metallib_path, and call quantized_matmul. Formats bridge exactly without repacking: onyx w=(q-8)*scale equals mlx q*scale+bias with biases=-8*scale. Repack the 2-nibbles-per-byte stream into uint32 words (8 nibbles/word, little-endian) once per layer and cache.
payload.when: Any Apple-Silicon engine that currently dequantizes weights or hand-rolls quantized GEMM.
payload.how: 1. Link libmlx.dylib; set_metallib_path before the first kernel. 2. Repack weights uint8->uint32 and build biases=-8*scales; eval and cache per layer. 3. Activations: convert via the copying float->float16 constructor (foreign-pointer zero-copy segfaults). 4. Output: read back through astype(float32)+eval; a direct fp16 data() read without sync returns garbage. 5. Gate by env for fallback (native|mlx|auto).
caveats: per-call costs remain: fp16->float activation conversion and fp32 read-back (~1 ms at m=1024)
mlx dynamic library and metallib versions must move together

entry.note: engine m1024 4.10 ms vs 8.4 ms own best public-API kernel (6.6x vs tile16 baseline); m16 decode 0.374 ms beats tile16 0.473 and python-mlx 0.726
